method: Independent full visible-DOM reading, required lambda/data operations, screenshots at960x720/320x420/640x240, and an actual reload to check the page's explicit persistence claim. No source or generation conditions read.
overall: A complete and usable derivation with correct requested numbers, diagrams, and degeneracy states. No error was found in the main optimizing argument or the required interaction. The narrow-screen number table splits values, and a claimed state-restoration feature did not work in the tested Reader.
strengths: Clearly distinguishes scaling the entire objective from averaging only the squared-error term while retaining lambda; the total convention is used consistently.

The centered residual identity, two zero sums, vanished cross term, and elimination of b are explained continuously. The subsequent reduced J(a) is explicitly identified as minimizing b for each a rather than holding b fixed.

The one-variable square completion establishes a unique minimum in a, then the nonnegative b term lifts the conclusion back to J(a,b). The Hessian and Sxx+lambda condition correctly support uniqueness.

All required numerical states match the mathematical reference. Dynamic equations, the current-data label, Hessian determinant, unique/nonunique text, scatterplot, and profile curve agree in the tested states and after return to normal data.

At degenerate lambda0 the drawn line family really passes through (2,1.6), the profile is horizontal at21.2, a is nonunique, and b is a relation. At positive lambda the unique horizontal line and curved profile appear correctly without claiming better SSE.

The two side-by-side desktop charts show vertical residuals and squared-residual areas separately from the objective profile; they support rather than replace the proof. The prescribed interaction sequence explicitly separates normal exploration from switching to degeneracy.
Prose and formula blocks remain readable at320px, and all controls work in320x420 and640x240 without fixed-layer obstruction.
